_comment: Phase 2C.4 hardware-assisted validation gate configuration. Consumed by tools/phase2c_hardware_gate.ps1. Docs/tooling artifact - not firmware source. Superset of tools/phase2b_hardware_gate_config.json (which remains frozen/untouched for the accepted Phase 2B-only baseline) - covers all 10 apps (8 Phase 2A/2B + 2 Phase 2C: sd_info, docviewlite) now in the accepted Phase 2C baseline. fcc_id_lookup is not part of this baseline - it remains deferred pending a license-evidence resolution and is intentionally absent from allowedApps below.

acceptedBaseline.note: This is the exact commit and CI evidence the Phase 2C acceptance record (docs/PHASE2C_3_ACCEPTANCE_RECORD.md) covers. Hardware-assisted validation against a different commit is not itself wrong, but should be flagged for review rather than silently treated as validating this same accepted baseline.

expectedArtifacts.note: These are the real, GitHub-Actions-generated values recorded in docs/PHASE2C_3_ARTIFACT_HASHES.md (Phase 2C.3, finalization run 28899393035) - not fabricated, not archive-level digests. HashVerify/HardwareAssisted modes compare a locally-downloaded artifact directory's actual files against these exact values.

expectedAppPrivateStoragePathsNote: null means the app is not expected to persist any file under normal use; any storage write by these apps outside their own entry (or any write at all, for the null-path apps) is a fail condition per the hardware smoke-test checklist. chess's and sudoku's paths are derived from source-code analysis in Phase 2A/2B (storage.h's APP_DATA_PATH macro + storage_processing.c's /data -> /ext/apps_data/<appid> mapping), not yet confirmed by an actual device/SD-card observation. sd_info and docviewlite are new to Phase 2C and are described in their own dedicated notes below rather than this generic null/path scheme, since neither fits the app-private-save-file pattern.
sdInfoStorageNote: sd_info is NOT zero-storage and NOT app-private, per the real source read in Phase 2C.1 (docs/PHASE2C_1_SOURCE_LICENSE_VERIFICATION.md) and Phase 2C.2 (docs/PHASE2C_2_SAFETY_REVIEW.md): its SD-card speed test writes, reads back, and deletes benchmark blocks at /ext/sdtest.tmp* (SD-card root, TEST_FILE_PATH = "/ext/sdtest.tmp"), 48 write/read/verify/delete cycles of 32KB blocks, ONLY when the user explicitly presses OK to start the test on the app's own test page. This is controlled, self-cleaning, and transient - not persistent, not automatic, not a safety-exclusion-list capability - but it is a real write to the SD-card root, materially different from an app-private save file or a read-only app. The hardware smoke-test checklist must confirm no /ext/sdtest.tmp* files remain after a normal test completion or after aborting mid-test.
docviewliteStorageNote: docviewlite is confirmed read-only by source (docs/PHASE2C_1_SOURCE_LICENSE_VERIFICATION.md, docs/PHASE2C_2_SAFETY_REVIEW.md): it opens and reads a user-selected .txt file via the standard Flipper file-browser dialog and storage_file_read only - no storage_file_write call exists anywhere in its source. The hardware smoke-test checklist should confirm no new file or modification appears anywhere on the SD card after using this app.
forbiddenTestCategories: Any cloning, brute force, jamming, deauth, or bypass behavior
forbiddenTestCategoriesNote: This script contains no code path for any of the above, for any app, under any flag or mode - this is not a configuration toggle to disable, it is simply not implemented anywhere in tools/phase2c_hardware_gate.ps1.
flashConfirmationPhrase: I UNDERSTAND THIS WILL FLASH THE CONNECTED DEVICE
flashConfirmationNote: The script never performs a flash itself under any circumstance - even after -AllowFlashPrompt and a correctly-typed confirmation phrase, flashing remains a manual, deliberate action performed by the operator using qFlipper or fbt flash_usb outside this script. The confirmation gate exists to make sure the operator has seen the artifact hashes and rollback warning before proceeding, not to automate the flash itself.

deviceDetection.note: Flipper Zero enumerates as a USB CDC-ACM serial device (ST Microelectronics VID 0483, PID 5740) when running normal firmware. Detection uses Windows PnP device enumeration (Get-PnpDevice) only - no serial communication, no RPC, no data exchange with the device.

officialToolingDetection.note: Best-effort detection only (PATH lookup, common install directories, and the Windows uninstall registry key). Absence of a detected install does not necessarily mean qFlipper isn't present under a nonstandard path - it means this script could not confirm it automatically, and flashing tooling should be classified BLOCKED / TOOLING NOT AVAILABLE rather than assumed present.

reportFilenameCollisionFix: Phase 2A's and Phase 2B's hardware gate scripts used second-granularity report filenames (yyyyMMdd_HHmmss), so two invocations within the same wall-clock second could silently overwrite each other's report - a real, documented, minor tooling limitation (see docs/PHASE2A_HARDWARE_ASSISTED_RESULTS.md and docs/PHASE2B_HARDWARE_ASSISTED_RESULTS.md). tools/phase2c_hardware_gate.ps1 fixes this for its own reports by using a millisecond-precision timestamp plus a short random hex suffix (yyyyMMdd_HHmmss_fff_XXXX) - collision-resistant even for rapid repeated invocations. Phase 2A's and Phase 2B's own scripts are deliberately left unmodified, per this phase's explicit instruction not to touch them.
